problem: For integers r>=2, k>=1, a_1..a_k>=1, b>=1 let P(q) = [a_1]_q...[a_k]_q * [b]_{q^r}, where [n]_q = 1+q+...+q^{n-1} and [b]_{q^r} = 1+q^r+...+q^{r(b-1)}. P is (weakly) unimodal if its coefficients satisfy c_0<=...<=c_m>=...>=c_N for some m. U = {b : P unimodal}, F = sum floor(a_i/r), D = sum(a_i-1). Question: exactly which parameters make P unimodal? (Source: arXiv:2605.12822, Conjecture 5.4.)

claims.statement: Lemma A1/A2 (window form of S2); Theorem B* (cross-pair transfer under decay hypothesis (H2) and shape condition (K*)) and Theorem B (sine form, residue-level certificate eps<1); Proposition D (obstruction): explicit palindromic log-concave sequences D1-D3 with e unimodal, Wintner sign pattern and cyclically unimodal Gamma violate S2, so S2 does not follow from these qualitative ingredients.
